author: Duval Times
title: Jacksonville launches merch store and scavenger hunt
text:
Donna Deegan - Mayor of Jacksonville, FL | City of Jacksonville website
Donna Deegan - Mayor of Jacksonville, FL | City of Jacksonville website
The City of Jacksonville has launched a new merchandise store and an accompanying scavenger hunt to engage residents and promote local pride. Mayor Donna Deegan stated, “This isn’t just any merch store; it’s a celebration of everything that makes Jacksonville bold, creative, and uniquely us.” The store offers locally designed items like t-shirts, hats, tumblers, and stickers that reflect the city’s growth and progress.
The idea for the merchandise originated from Jacksonville residents who expressed interest in "I Dig Jax"-branded products featuring Rex the Dinosaur, the campaign's mascot. The city partnered with reputable U.S. companies offering print-on-demand services to avoid using taxpayer dollars for inventory or order fulfillment. According to city ordinance, profits from sales will support marketing efforts for citywide events.
To generate excitement about the new store, a scavenger hunt has been organized. Over five weeks, miniature 3D-printed Rex statues will be hidden around Duval County. Residents can follow clues on the city's social media channels to participate in this initiative. The statues were created by Forge 3D Studios, a Jacksonville-based company.
